headline: California's 4:15 Dinner Dilemma Escalates into National Crisis
deck: In a state where the sun sets early, so does civility—over salad.
article:
In a twist that could only happen in California, the cherished 4:15 PM dinner time has erupted into a political firestorm, pitting early diners against the late-night snackers of the world. A petition for 'Dinner Time Equality,' now boasting over 10,000 signatures, has caught the attention of lawmakers, who are being urged to push for a more inclusive 5:30 PM dining hour for the beleaguered foodies of the Golden State. Governor Marlene Fiddlesticks has taken a bold step by proposing a 'Dinner Time Amendment' to align California with Boston's mealtime norms, aiming to unite all Californians under one culinary banner.

In an effort to bridge this culinary divide, the state hosted a 'Dinner Time Summit,' where bewildered diners mingled with chefs serving an exquisitely cold salad. This dish, a chilling metaphor for division, was drizzled with dressing that symbolized the bitterness festering within the state legislature. Legislator Vincent Broccoli quipped, "If we cannot break bread together, at least let us share a bowl of lettuce."

As chaos brews across state lines—complete with a culinary embargo halting mayonnaise shipments into California—the nation watches in disbelief. The House of Representatives has awkwardly scheduled a series of hearings on synchronized dining, set to occur between 3:45 PM and 4:05 PM. With tensions simmering like an overcooked casserole, experts warn that this salad may just be the appetizer for a full-blown culinary crisis, ripe for the picking.
author: Samantha Mealton, Senior Culinary Correspondent

oped.title: A Culinary Catastrophe: Why California's Salad Standoff is the New Civil War
oped.author: Bartholomew D. Hattinator, Culinary Crisis Consultant
oped.body: As we navigate the absurdity of California's 4:15 Dinner Dilemma, we must ponder: when did a simple salad become a battleground for civility? It’s time to point fingers, and I suggest we start with the floppy hats of California diners. Clearly, those brims are blocking not just the sun but their common sense! They say a well-dressed salad is a happy salad, but I argue a well-hatted Californian has never met a decent fork. The solution? Mandatory hat inspections at every restaurant entry. Yes, folks! Let’s make dining fashionable again by enforcing the most ludicrous dress code ever imagined. And if they refuse to don a sensible hat? 4:15 becomes lunchtime, and we’ll serve them tuna salad sandwiches! This is the new America! Remove the hats and watch civility rise like sourdough at dawn. One hat at a time, we reclaim the dinner table!

classifieds.text: Selling exclusive collection of 4:15 PM dinner plates—never been used! Perfect for those who want to dine early without judgment. Act fast, before California's dinner hour is ushered into a new time zone!

Wanted: Emergency Salad Mediator for escalating dinner conflicts in California. Must be trained in immediate conflict resolution and have experience with anxiety-ridden diners. Flexible hours (4:15 PM preferred).
LOST: Last shred of civility, last seen during a heated argument over croutons at the 4:15 PM dinner. If found, please return to the nearest Kumbaya Café where forgiveness is served daily at 4:16 PM.

Apologies to all California residents for the sudden shift in dinner decorum. We understand that eating salad in silence with glaring side-eyes isn’t sustainable. Let’s reconvene for a ‘Let’s Talk About It’ brunch—at 10:15 AM, naturally.

stories.headline: Massachusetts Coffee Chains Introduce 'Pre-Caffeine' Hour
stories.deck: Finally, a solution that suits everyone’s circadian chaos.
stories.article:
In response to California's ongoing 4:15 Dinner Dilemma, several Massachusetts coffee chains have rolled out a new 'Pre-Caffeine' hour, allowing patrons to sip overpriced lattes before their regularly scheduled breakfast at 11:02 AM. Under this innovative policy, customers are encouraged to indulge in existential conversations while waiting for their French croissants, which, in a twist of irony, also arrive 60 minutes late due to supply chain disruptions.

A spokesperson for the Dunkin' Decelerator franchise proclaimed, 'Offering coffee an hour before breakfast is just as revolutionary as merging lunch and dinner, but without the societal wreckage.' However, California residents have begun protesting this policy, demanding an immediate shift to 'Pre-Dinner' cocktails at 2:00 PM.

stories.headline: The Great Boston Time-Lock Festival Set for Next Saturday
stories.deck: Expect a confusing medley of synchronized celebrations and missed appointments.
stories.article:
The annual Boston Time-Lock Festival is set for a full 12 hours of chaotic overlap between events, all occurring simultaneously across the country. This festival, dedicated to the bewildering concept of clashing activities, promises 'Simultaneous Barbecuing' alongside 'Early Bird Yoga' sessions, allowing participants to critically assess the existential dread of preparing dinner at 8:15 AM.

Event organizers are urging participants to arrive promptly despite the unique conditions. 'Time is a social construct, and so is commitment,' stated lead organizer Jim Chronos, who later revealed plans for an impromptu demonstration of all missed appointments since the festival's inception in 1987.
